source.title: The Shape of the DPO Hyperparameter Landscape: What to Measure, How It Moves with Scale, and When Not to Transfer It
source.authors: H. Mahadik; David Salinas; Jacek Golebiowski; Aaron Klein

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses pretraining scaling laws as context and tests DPO hyperparameter selection across model sizes, but it does not test the claim’s pretraining loss laws, extrapolation, compute-optimal parameter/token allocation, architecture-shape effect, or downstream predictability from pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Kaplan et al. and Hoffmann et al. and describes its DPO scale analysis as analogous but different. Its own results concern DPO hyperparameter rankings and transfer, not held-out pretraining loss scaling. The DPO learning-rate and preference-data results below are recorded as adjacent findings under fits_no_version; they do not test a listed claim version.
record.test_reason: The study tunes DPO learning rate and β across Qwen3 sizes and measures downstream rankings and transfer regret. It cites Kaplan et al. and Hoffmann et al. only as context for hyperparameter-transfer work. It reports no pretraining or fine-tuning loss as a function of parameters, tokens or compute. It fits no power law; the authors call the learning-rate trend fit descriptive, not a scaling law. It does not relate downstream performance to scale or pretraining loss, so no claim version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that DPO hyperparameter selection depends on target model, preference data and evaluation objective, and that validation loss is a poor selection signal. The selected Qwen3 learning rate declines overall with scale, but its small-scale rise and boundary β selections argue against a universal configuration or simple transfer rule. Partial runs (20–30% of training) give useful ranking information.
record.recipe_differences: The study performs DPO hyperparameter sweeps and transfer analyses rather than measuring pretraining loss scaling or compute-optimal pretraining allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: DPO configuration rankings and selections vary with model size, preference dataset, and evaluation objective; the two chat judges disagree at Qwen3-0.6B.

fits_no_version.finding: The best observed ZAll DPO learning rate rises from 0.6B to 1.7B, then falls through 14B (Table 11). Per-size response-surface estimates under ZDynamic show the same rise-then-fall (Fig. 4). The selected learning rate also differs by objective, e.g. at 8B ZDynamic picks 4e-7 and ZStatic picks 4e-6.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimal DPO learning rate declines overall with model size within Qwen3, but non-monotonically and objective-dependently; no simple transfer rule.

fits_no_version.finding: Dolci-to-UltraFeedback ZAll transfer regret is 0.00, 0.25, 0.67, 1.00 and 1.00 from Qwen3-0.6B to 14B (Table 12).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: DPO configuration transfer across preference datasets becomes consequential at larger Qwen3 sizes.

record.problems: The five-size scale analysis is confined to Qwen3; the grids are finite and some selected values lie at tested boundaries. Each DPO configuration uses one training seed, so the reported analysis does not measure training-seed variance. Preference-data sensitivity is tested with only one alternative dataset. The Llama models are not a homogeneous scaling series.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were omitted under the row cap.

untested.parts: All: no pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
All: no fitted loss law is extrapolated to larger runs.
All: no compute-optimal parameter or token allocation.
All: no depth or width comparisons at fixed parameter count.
All: DPO post-training is studied, but no power law in loss or performance with scale is fitted or tested.
All: downstream scores are used to rank hyperparameters within each size, not related to scale or pretraining loss.
All: no scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal splits are fitted.

record.verdict_notes: The paper's only link to the phenomenon is a related-work sentence citing Kaplan and Hoffmann. The authors say the fitted learning-rate line is not a scaling law or a predictor for unseen sizes. Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only' because the claim's validity is not discussed. Rows r1–r4 carry the ZDynamic label but hold ZAll values; the reader's first fits_no_version entry repeats this mislabel.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a power law in parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger-run pretraining loss from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation for pretraining, including how either scales with compute.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture details on loss at fixed parameter count.
Whether the pretraining power-law form holds in other modalities or training regimes.
Predictability of downstream task performance from scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of pretraining scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal allocations on fitting choices, or departures of pretraining loss curves from a single power law.
